tob-4244: T. W. Rolleston’s broad survey strings the myths of Ireland, Scotland, Wales, and Brittany into one flowing tale. From the Tuatha Dé Danann to Cuchulain to Arthur’s borderland, he retells them with a poet’s heart. The book stays the most readable one-volume Celtic myth-book.
tob-4144: Ralph Griffith’s Ramayana gives book one of Valmiki’s great epic — Rama’s forest exile, Sita’s stealing, and war begun with the fiend Ravana. His 1870 verse-Englishing bore India’s beloved tale to English readers. The epic’s high heart and ruth shine through.
tob-13144: Swami Vivekananda’s Bhakti Yoga teaches the road of love-godliness — oneness with God through love, worship, and self-yielding. His talks made India’s heart-worship open to western readers. The book crowns his fourfold yoga word. It stays a beloved guide to the heart’s yoga.
arxiv-2605-08844: Rough path theory extends calculus to jagged, irregular signals, and kernel equations from physics fit naturally inside it. Thomas Cass, Dan Crisan, Andrea Iannucci, and William F. Turner recast signature-kernel and Schwinger-Dyson equations as two-parameter rough differential equations. The 2026 paper is stochastic analysis uniting machine-learning kernels with field-theory tools.
arxiv-2605-09044: Continual-learning models must stay plastic — able to learn new things — without forgetting the old. Jiuqi Wang, Jayanth Srinivasa, Claire Chen, and Shuze Daniel Liu develop theory for predicting plasticity in deep continual learning. The 2026 paper asks when a network keeps its ability to learn.
arxiv-2605-09844: Do language models know what they don't know? Rafael C. T. Oliveira probes their self-knowledge with five behavioural calibration diagnostics — the metacognitive probe. The 2026 paper tests AI self-awareness rigorously, one careful diagnostic at a time. It is introspection, automated.
arxiv-2605-10344: Test-time compute scaled via multi-agent synergy — TMAS multiplies minds at inference. George Wu, Nan Jing, Qing Yi, and colleagues build the system. The 2026 paper is LLM inference scaled socially. It scales test-time compute through genuine multi-agent synergy.
arxiv-2605-10444: Urea interacting with bovine serum albumin in an acid-expanded conformation — the molecular mechanisms. Y. Ricardo Espinosa, C. Manuel Carlevaro, C. Gastón Ferrara, and colleagues simulate them. The 2026 paper is biophysics. It simulates urea unfolding bovine serum albumin at the molecular level.
arxiv-2605-10544: Long-context supervision — where does it actually go? Effective-context exposure balancing answers. Jinchang Zhu, Jindong Li, Chengyu Zou, and colleagues develop the balancing. The 2026 paper is LLM training. It tracks supervision through the long context. Exposure balanced. Supervision finds its place.
pmc-13407944: Colorectal cancer patients facing surgery — predicting who will gain functional capacity from pre-surgery prehabilitation, in a retrospective study. M. de Klerk, M. J. pmc-13421244: Hydrogen solubility in chemicals — predicted with a QSPR-based machine learning approach, comparatively studied. Ali Ebrahimpoor Gorji and Ville Alopaeus build the models. pmc-13569544: Postoperative adjuvant S-1 chemotherapy for gastric cancer — continuous pharmacist intervention maintaining dose intensity, in a multicenter study. pmc-13571344: Transradial PCI — a fragment of radial arterial wall avulsed and embolizing the coronary artery. Raid Faraj, Sebastien Hess, Xavier Lamit, and colleagues report the complication. pmc-13455644: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential and cancer — their causal association tested by Mendelian randomization. Juan Jin, Qian Pu, Chengrong Wu, and colleagues run the genetics. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is CHIP epidemiology. It asks whether mutant blood clones cause cancer.
pmc-13446344: Artificial intelligence in the EU Safe Hearts Plan — prediction alone is not enough. Hannah van Kolfschooten, Georges Hattab, Franziska Bächler, and colleagues make the argument. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is AI health policy. It demands more than prediction from heart AI.
pmc-13403044: Rural Afghan women's postnatal care — service utilization and associated factors, from the 2022-2023 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey. arxiv-2606-17244: Kazi Parvez Islam and colleagues tune the magnetism of a double perovskite, Nd2-xSrxCoMnO6, by controlling antisite disorder, atoms sitting on the wrong lattice sites. arxiv-2606-17344: Yurou Liu and colleagues explain how wide binary companions drive planets into scorching close orbits. arxiv-2606-17444: Yifang Liang and colleagues dissect GRB 250424A, a gamma-ray burst showing energy injection, with multiwavelength observations. arxiv-2606-18044: Andrea Panarotto and colleagues cluster compositional trajectories to analyze mobility data. arxiv-2606-18144: Josef Chen treats memory as a wasting asset, pricing flash endurance for embodied agents and probing the limits of doing. arxiv-2606-18244: Fergus Donnan and colleagues map polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons at cosmic noon with JWST's MIRI spectrometer in PAHSPECS. plos-pone-0003444: Immunologists watched evolution happen inside patients in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003544: Cancer researchers isolated the roots of a deadly thyroid tumor in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003644: In 2008, a team studied faulty calcium control in weak muscle. plos-pone-0003744: In 2008, Wimberly, Hildreth, and Boyte asked why West Nile lingers on the northern plains. Mapping the 2003 epidemic's ecological niche, they found the landscape and climate factors keeping risk high there. The niche map explains a regional hotspot of a national disease.
plos-pone-0003844: In 2008, Shaw, Lindholm, and Prajsnar discovered a new stress chief in staph bacteria. Sigma S, a novel component of Staphylococcus aureus stress and virulence control, was identified and characterized. The finding adds a master switch to the portrait of a formidable pathogen.
plos-pone-0003944: In 2008, Habuchi, Tsutsui, and Kochaniak introduced mKikGR, a single-chain light switch. The monomeric photoswitchable fluorescent protein can be toggled on and off for imaging. The compact tool expands the palette for tracking molecules in living cells.
plos-pone-0004044: In 2008, Adrian Melott found a slow pulse in the history of life. Fossil data showed marine biodiversity rising and falling on a 63-million-year cycle. The striking periodicity emerged from the Paleobiology Database's vast fossil record. The 63-million-year beat hints at a cosmic or geological metronome behind evolution.
plos-pone-0004144: In 2009, Lu, Lin, and Kuo linked diabetes to faster aging. Their review tied diabetes to cognitive, mobility, and mood decline. The pooled studies covered many aging signs. Diabetes emerged as a whole-body aging driver. The pattern urges earlier screening in diabetic patients.
plos-pone-0004244: In 2009, Fernandez, Fu, and Pascual measured Spain's smoke-free law. The Spanish smoking ban cut second-hand smoke exposure in hospitality venues. plos-pone-0004344: In 2009, Kenny, Ward, and Josefsson found staph surviving human skin's natural oil. Staphylococcus aureus countered unsaturated long-chain free fatty acids well. The germ's survival tricks and virulence shifts were mapped fully. The neat finding exposes a chink in staph's armor.
plos-pone-0004444: In 2009, Gálvez, San Martín, and Rodríguez found inflammation calling in reinforcements. TNF-alpha attracted mesenchymal precursors to white adipose tissue in obese mice. plos-pone-0004544: In 2009, Solé, Bonifaci, and López-Bigas found cancer gene lists largely agreeing. Biological convergence of cancer signatures was demonstrated. plos-pone-0004644: In 2009, Choi, Beattie, and Bryson argued big trials may miss a pain technique's value. Effects of neuraxial blockade may be difficult to study using large randomized trials. The rare complications need huge samples. The paper informs trial design. The blockade is spinal.
plos-pone-0004744: In 2009, a team found cat leukemia threatening the Iberian lynx anew here. Cat leukemia virus and other germs hit the rare wild cat. The captive breeding program fought back fast. The study informs wildlife rescue efforts. The lynx is Earth's rarest cat.
plos-pone-0358644: Ringing ears and low mood travel together — but do the questionnaires measuring them ask the same questions twice? This paper used the ICF framework to analyze the overlap between tinnitus distress and depression questionnaires. Mapping the shared content helps clinicians avoid double-counting symptoms.
plos-pone-0358444: In the lava fields of northwest Saudi Arabia stand mustatils — mysterious Neolithic stone structures. plos-pone-0358044: Telling ‘la’ from ‘ra’ — or ‘ba’ from ‘ga’ — is genuinely hard for young ears. This exploratory fNIRS brain-imaging study tested directional asymmetry in segmental discrimination in young children. The results reveal how developing brains sort similar sounds, with implications for language learning and therapy.
plos-pone-0356544: Breakthrough infections and imperfect vaccines don’t just fail individuals — they drive pathogen evolution. This paper showed breakthrough infections and incomplete vaccine efficacy drive immune escape in pathogens. The finding is a warning: leaky protection can breed evasive variants.
plos-pone-0352744: Classifying desert rangeland plants from drones — with only a handful of examples — is brutally hard. MetaMamba combines meta-learning with mamba state-space models for few-shot vegetation species classification using UAV hyperspectral imagery. The AI maps fragile desert rangelands that ground surveys can’t reach.
plos-pone-0355844: The African sugarcane stalk borer — Eldana saccharina — tunnels through profits across Tanzania. This study examined the factors affecting infestation status of the pest in Tanzanian cane fields. The findings give growers and extension workers an evidence-based guide to managing one of sugar’s costliest enemies.
plos-pone-0355044: Educational professionals need reliable ways to assess theory of mind-related skills in children with autism. This paper designed, developed, and pilot-tested exactly such a scale. The new tool helps teachers understand how autistic children read minds — and tailor support accordingly.
plos-pone-0357044: Henan Province’s vegetation has shifted dramatically since 2000. This paper monitored those changes through 2023 and analyzed the driving factors behind them. The two-decade trends give land managers the evidence to protect what’s greening — and restore what’s browning.
plos-pone-0356244: Computer-aided detection could find more tuberculosis cases in Ghana — but is it worth the money? This decision-analytic modeling study assessed the cost-effectiveness of CAD for TB in the Ghanaian context. The analysis gives health officials the numbers to decide whether to invest.
plos-pone-0342144: Weight-based mistreatment at work — fat shaming on the job — is finally being studied. This exploratory study investigated the correlates of experiencing it. The findings name a form of workplace discrimination that has hidden in plain sight.
plos-pone-0356644: Pancreatic cancer striking women of childbearing age is a cruel and understudied tragedy. This paper quantified the burden of early-onset pancreatic cancer and its association with risk factors in this group. The findings expose which risks matter most for young women — knowledge that could sharpen both prevention and early detection.
plos-pone-0353944: Female volleyball players with dynamic knee valgus — knees collapsing inward on landing — face high ACL tear risk. This protocol outlines a randomized controlled trial of neuromuscular-cognitive training to reduce those risk factors. The planned trial tests whether training both body and brain can keep young athletes’ knees intact.
plos-pone-0355744: HIV patients with persistent low-level viremia face a dilemma: switch regimens or stay the course? This multicenter retrospective Chinese cohort study examined antiretroviral regimen switching and short-term viral suppression. The real-world data guide one of HIV care’s most common and consequential decisions.
plos-pone-0356144: Leishmania parasites smuggle molecular messages into human immune cells via exosomes. This quantitative proteomic analysis showed the parasites’ exosomal tRNA-derived small RNAs modulate proteins in THP-1-derived macrophages. The smuggled RNAs reveal a sophisticated parasite strategy — and potential drug targets.
plos-pone-0345444: Urban infrastructure supply chains snap under stress — unless predictive analytics sees the break coming. This paper applied graph convolutional networks to supply chain resilience in urban infrastructure networks. The network-based predictions give city planners early warnings about which supply links will fail when disaster strikes.
plos-pone-0336744: Elderly South Koreans from rural regions flock to Seoul’s hospitals — a concentration the pandemic tested. This paper measured hospital utilization concentration in the capital among elderly inpatients from non-capital regions, before and during COVID-19. The findings expose regional healthcare inequality that the virus only sharpened.
plos-pone-0355544: Female university students faced the pandemic with fear — and coped in varied ways. This paper examined fear and coping strategies, testing physical activity and infection status as moderators. The findings show what buffered young women’s mental health when the world shut down.
plos-pone-0355944: Tracking Legionella — the pneumonia-causing bacterium — in the environment needs fast, accessible genomics. This paper achieved rapid, consistent genetic clustering of environmental Legionella pneumophila isolates using accessible single-step whole-genome sequencing tools. The streamlined workflow brings genomic epidemiology within reach of ordinary labs.
plos-pone-0354744: Eye health systems need complete profiles — beyond prevalence numbers. This paper built one using rapid assessment of avoidable blindness, a population-based eye health survey, and facility data. The comprehensive profile gives health planners the full picture — from blindness rates to service capacity.
plos-pone-0352244: Drones surveying cluttered landscapes must spot tiny objects — vehicles, people, animals — against visual noise. This paper built a robust small-object detection model for UAV aerial imagery under complex background clutter. The hardened detector promises reliable aerial surveillance where backgrounds conspire to hide what matters.
plos-pone-0355244: This entry is a retraction notice, not a research finding. The journal has retracted the global systematic review and meta-analysis comparing integrated palliative care versus standard care on quality of life in cancer patients. The notice formally withdraws those findings from the scientific record.
plos-pone-0354344: Older adults facing leg-saving surgery for chronic limb-threatening ischemia — prehabilitation might improve their odds. The POCI study protocol outlines a multicenter trial of a multimodal multicomponent prehabilitation program. The planned research tests whether preparing body and mind before surgery saves limbs — and lives.
plos-pone-0350044: Soil texture classification and crop recommendation — by lightweight AI. AgriOptNet fuses hybrid optimization with efficient deep learning for both tasks based on soil nutrition. plos-pone-0351644: Settlements from Neolithic to Bronze Age — 9000 to 3000 years ago — in China’s Songshan Mountain region. This paper traced their spatiotemporal evolution and clustering. The six-millennium analysis revealed how communities grew, moved, and concentrated. The findings illuminate Chinese civilization’s deep roots — villages becoming the foundations of states.
plos-pone-0353244: Steel tube-stud grouting connectors — small-diameter, novel — their anti-pull performance tested. This paper researched it. The mechanical testing revealed how these connectors resist extraction forces. The findings enable slimmer, stronger structural connections — engineering for the next generation of composite structures.
plos-pone-0353844: Deblurring signals and images — via a two-step iterative framework using G-I-nonexpansive mappings. This paper built it. The mathematical framework sharpened what blur obscured. The findings advance the inverse mathematics behind every deblurred photo and clarified signal.
plos-pone-0354244: Fruit peel biowaste — transformed into sustainable hydrogels from pectin and starch. This paper synthesized and characterized them. The waste-derived materials absorbed and released on demand. The findings turned garbage into functional materials — the circular economy made tangible.
plos-pone-0354144: Tea genotypes tolerating waterlogging — assessed morpho-physiologically and biochemically. This paper profiled them. The multi-level assessment revealed which teas survive drowning. The findings guide breeding for the flood-prone gardens where climate change is rewriting the rules of tea cultivation.
plos-pone-0351744: Historic cities’ public spaces — sustainably designed via space syntax analysis. This paper applied that approach. The configurational analysis revealed how street networks shape social life. The findings guide preservation that keeps old cities alive — heritage as lived space, not museum.
plos-pone-0353744: Lung adenocarcinoma — a novel lncRNA RP3-340N1.2 and its miR-4650-5p/SHC1 regulatory network. This paper characterized both. The findings mapped a noncoding RNA circuit driving lung cancer. The research nominated new biomarkers and targets — the dark genome illuminating oncology.
plos-pone-0353344: Mechanically ventilated patients — nurse-led targeted sedation-analgesia management associated with ventilation duration and quality. This paper did so. The findings showed nursing protocols shortening intubation. The research empowered the bedside — nurses steering sedation, patients breathing sooner. The nurse-led design is the point: it shifts sedation management from physician orders to protocol-driven bedside nursing judgment.
plos-pone-0347744: Chinese higher education — high-quality development evaluated with spatial layout. This paper researched it. The findings mapped excellence’s geography. The research informed the policy — the universities’ quality, placed. The spatial layout is the insight: it reveals which provinces concentrate quality and which are left behind.
plos-pone-0352344: Australian COVID-19 patients — respiratory and bloodstream coinfections and antimicrobial use in a retrospective cohort. This paper studied them. The findings quantified the co-infections of moderate to severe disease. The research guided the stewardship — the antibiotics, justified or not.
plos-pone-0352944: This entry is a retraction notice, not a research finding. It retracts the paper claiming the succinate receptor GPR91 is involved in pressure overload-induced ventricular hypertrophy. plos-pone-0351944: Industrial cooling towers — data-driven prediction and thermodynamic performance assessment via advanced machine learning. This paper built the models. plos-pone-0351844: Silver-selenium nanocomposite — biogenic, with anticancer activity and potent efficacy against vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus. This paper created it. The biogenic synthesis is the green chemistry: microbes manufacture the nanoparticles, avoiding the toxic reagents of conventional routes.
plos-pone-0352644: Prosthetic ankle-foot devices — evidence-based prescription through a multisite randomized crossover trial. This paper ran it. plos-pone-0352444: Managed beech forests — short-term rewetting after summer drought not altering fungal communities or manganese peroxidase activity. This paper demonstrated the null. The analysis tested the forest floor’s resilience. Its ecological value is the negative. The work finds the fungi unmoved by the rain’s return.
plos-pone-0352144: Climate-smart cropping — data-driven strategies boosting yield while minimizing greenhouse gases through optimized systems and fertilization. This paper developed them. The analysis balanced the harvest against the emissions. The finding serves the warming fields. The work farms more with less footprint.
plos-pone-0341344: Youth soccer players — horizontal jump inter-limb asymmetry’s test-retest reliability and sensitivity across maturity stages. This paper studied them. The analysis measured the jump’s consistency as boys grow. The finding validates the asymmetry. The work trusts the hop, developmentally. The maturity-stage lens is the development: it accounts for growth spurts that confound raw asymmetry measures.
europmc-pmc2816644: Tumors starved of oxygen turn on a characteristic set of genes, and this 2010 paper distills it. By pooling data across many cancers, the authors define a compact hypoxia metagene that strongly predicts patient survival. One signature works across tumor types. The metagene gave oncologists a single, powerful readout of tumor oxygen starvation.
europmc-pmc2846344: Leptin is famous for signaling fullness, but it also talks to the immune system. This 2010 review examines the role of leptin in activating immune cells. europmc-pmc2860244: A companion study widens the Oct4 web further. This 2010 paper presents an expanded Oct4 interaction network and draws out what it means for stem cell biology, development, and disease. The authors' bigger map deepens the picture. europmc-pmc2901944: Wound infections after surgery cost more than the hospital stay. This 2003 paper measures the health and money toll of surgical site infections found after patients go home. europmc-pmc2907344: Cancer drugs that save lives can wound hearts. This 2010 review pools randomized trials to weigh heart harm from anthracycline drugs, a mainstay of chemo. The authors pin down how often the damage strikes and who is at risk. Their numbers guide safer chemo choices for patients.
europmc-pmc2913244: Cells marching together need to touch to stay oriented. This 2010 paper shows group movement toward signals needs contact-based cell polarity. The authors reveal the touching rule behind group migration. Their work matters for wound healing and cancer spread alike.
europmc-pmc2939644: Stress scales need testing across cultures to travel well. This 2010 paper validates three versions of the Perceived Stress Scale in Chinese heart patients who smoke. The authors confirm the tool works across languages. Their work aids cross-cultural stress research.
europmc-pmc2954944: Scoping studies map research territory, and this 2010 paper sharpens the method. The authors advance scoping study methodology. Their framework guides evidence mappers. europmc-pmc2970544: A pork tapeworm larva causes epilepsy worldwide, and this 2010 review counts the burden. europmc-pmc2993644: Unnecessary C-sections harm mothers, this 2010 WHO survey finds. The authors link surgery without medical need to worse short-term outcomes for mothers across countries. europmc-pmc3019144: Losing one copy of an autism gene breaks mouse sociability. This 2010 study shows mice missing one Shank3 copy suffer faulty synapses and poor social skills. The authors model the disorder. Their work clarifies autism biology. The findings mirror human Phelan-McDermid syndrome.
europmc-pmc3056144: Protein models need their hydrogens placed. This 2009 paper brings Protonate3D, a tool that adds missing hydrogens to protein models. europmc-pmc3069744: Diffraction data got an auto toolbox. This 2011 paper covers the autoPROC pipeline for processing crystal data. The authors' automation sped crystallography. europmc-pmc3087144: Preeclampsia shadows newborns too. This 2011 paper tracks how mothers' preeclampsia shapes babies' health. The authors reveal the newborn risks. Their work guides delivery care. europmc-pmc3156644: Bad muscle repair led to scarring. This 2011 paper covers how faulty repair drives fibrosis in skeletal muscle. The authors map the scarring process. Their overview guides therapy. Old muscles scarred instead of healing. Anti-scar drugs are now in trials.
europmc-pmc3164644: A tree-killing worm's genome got decoded. This 2011 paper sequences the pinewood nematode to trace parasitism's origins. The authors reveal stolen genes. europmc-pmc3169444: Seniors' step goals got set. This 2011 paper asks how many daily steps older adults need. The authors set the targets. Their work guides programs. Seven thousand steps sufficed, they found. Chronic-disease groups got tailored goals. The paper shaped senior fitness plans.
europmc-pmc3240744: Cell trash cans got their motor link mapped. This 2011 paper shows Arl8 and SKIP hook lysosomes to the kinesin motor. The authors reveal the coupling. Their work lights up cell biology. The link positions lysosomes precisely. Broken links cause nerve disease.
europmc-pmc3262844: Network clustering got a plugin. This 2011 paper brings clusterMaker, a multi-algorithm clustering plugin for Cytoscape. The authors' tool groups the networks. europmc-pmc3285644: Spinal cord surgery timing got tested. This 2012 STASCIS trial compares early versus late spinal decompression. The authors reveal the benefit. Their work guides surgeons. europmc-pmc3329544: Probiotic gut claims got pooled. This 2012 meta-analysis pools trials of probiotics for gut diseases. The authors grade the evidence. Their work guides doctors. Diarrhea showed the clearest benefit. Ritchie's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped prescribing.
europmc-pmc3400644: A short depression scale got validated. This 2012 paper validates a 10-question depression scale for HIV patients. The authors reveal the validation. Their work guides clinics. europmc-pmc3441244: Bubble removal got a cancer helper. This 2012 paper proposes filtering exosomes from blood as cancer help. The authors outline the idea. Their work points to trials. Marleau's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. Trials followed, they note.
europmc-pmc6514244: Standard DNA sequencing reads short fragments, which struggles with big rearrangements - the large insertions, deletions, and repeats behind many genetic disorders. europmc-pmc6710244: Period-tracking apps quietly amassed one of the largest reproductive datasets ever - over 600,000 cycles. europmc-pmc6723444: Building muscle takes protein - but does the source matter? europmc-pmc6739444: Bone marrow is a nursery for blood stem cells - and aging remodels the nursery. In premature-aging models, this study shows the stem-cell niche gets rewired, pushing myeloid cell expansion. The niche, not just the stem cells, drives the aging of blood.
europmc-pmc6790244: Cancer cells that morph and migrate are the deadly ones - and an RNA tag helps them do it. This study shows METTL3-driven m6A modification pushes epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis. Blocking the tag writer could keep tumors pinned in place.
europmc-pmc6818444: Science runs on trust - and trust needs rules. These updated ethical guidelines set the standards for credit and papers in the Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle and its twin journals. The guardrails keep the literature clean. Good ethics make good science possible.
europmc-pmc6857444: Beating cancer can cost the heart - years later. This population study tracked medium and long-term cardiovascular risks in survivors of 20 adult cancers. The findings flag which survivors need heart watch. Survival is step one; the heart is step two.
